newsitem.title: GERMANY: NordLB sees 1996 operating profit down 10 percent.
newsitem.headline: NordLB sees 1996 operating profit down 10 percent.

text.p: Norddeutsche Landesbank, a publicly owned German regional bank, said it expected operating profit after risk provisions to fall 10 percent to about 400 million marks ($256.4 million) in 1996.

The bank, which will next year start talks with Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG about a possible merger, said the earnings fall was explained by a rise in costs amid heavy investment in electronic data processing systems.

In the first 10 months of 1996, operating profit after risk provisions fell 15.3 percent to 318.2 million marks as administration costs rose 10 percent to 1.0 billion, chief executive Manfred Bodin told a news conference.
Looking ahead to 1997, Bodin said NordLB faced increased pressure on margins and would have to maintain high investments while risks in its loan portfolio remained.
He predicted NordLB would grow 6.7 percent to 223 billion marks by the end of 1996 from 208.9 billion in 1995. Business was likely to grow by six percent in 1997.
The lending volume is likely to rise to 133.5 billion marks by the end of 1996, up 5.7 percent from 1995, Bodin said.
